Subject: Hands-on kickoff: scheduling, reschedule option, and test payload checklist

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Wed like to lock in a 2-hour hands-on working session to kick off the POC and run through: prompt review, routing behavior, and a short load test (baseline QPS). Proposed scope:
- 30m: high-level goals and evaluation metrics (product + engineering)
- 60m: live prompt review + routing/playback of sample payloads
- 30m: light load run (scripted, short duration) + next steps

Proposed times (PDT):
- Tue, Jul 14 — 10:0012:00
- Wed, Jul 15 — 14:00:16:00

If those don't work, happy to move to Thu morning. Please confirm attendees and well send a calendar invite.

A couple asks to make the session productive:
1) Can you upload (or attach) a small sample set (1050) of representative prompts/payloads we can use during the review? Ideally CSV/JSON with one prompt per row and an approximate expected token count. Redact any PII.
2) Tell us expected concurrent QPS and typical payload sizes (KB) so Dev can size the load run.
3) Any routing rules you want exercised (e.g., route by customer tier, language, or endpoint)? If yes, a short matrix is helpful.

I attached a lightweight template (redwood_payload_template.csv) to speed up collection. If you prefer, drop files into the Drive folder linked below.

Thanks — looking forward.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Perfect — Wed, Jul 15 11:00:13:00 PDT works for us. Ill finalize the invite once Dev confirms the short load-run window.

Quick notes for the session and to set expectations:
- Redaction: the CSV looks fine at a glance. Please replace any free-text PII (names, emails) with tokens like [REDACTED_NAME]. We can accept hashed IDs instead of raw customer IDs.
- Routing matrix: if you can provide a simple CSV mapping (field, condition, target-route) we'll exercise that. If not, we can simulate a couple of common rules (language and product_area).
- Load test: plan is to run a 3-minute scripted ramp up to the QPS you provide, then a 2-minute steady window. This is intentionally short to avoid service disruption. Please tell us expected steady QPS and average payload size (KB).

Dev — can you confirm well be able to run the short scripted load during the session (well give you 48 hours to review the seed payload), and whether you need any specific SSH keys / IP allowlist entries from Acme? Also see attached routing_matrix_example.json for the format we use in the lab.

Alex — Marissa will coordinate the calendar and procurement follow-ups after we confirm the invite.

Thanks,
Sean

+1 on Wed 7/15 11:00 PDT. We can run the short scripted load during the session. A couple of technical notes for Acme (ccd here via earlier thread):

- Load harness: well run a client-side harness that replays the CSV rows at configured concurrency. No production keys are used; well use a staging key with strict rate caps.
- IP allowlist: if you want us to hit an endpoint in your environment (private), well need one or more /32 entries. For standard Redwood-hosted endpoints, nothing needed.
- Expected capacity: For the 3-minute ramp + 2-minute steady run we can handle up to 250 QPS with the default staging footprint. If you expect >250 QPS well provision a short burst node but need 2448h lead time.
- Payload sizing: your CSV looks reasonable; please add a column "approx_tokens" or "avg_kb" to each row. We use rough token estimates to choose batching.

Links/refs for the session:
- Playbook folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-playbook
- Load-run config template: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1load-config

I attached a sample routing matrix and a quick README. Ill prep the staging key and the short run script this week.

—Dev
